overall: The AG found the Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the August 10 topic listing for the Claremont special permit was sufficiently specific. Hearing-notice and document-provision claims were declined as non-violations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the August 10 notice topic for a developer's special permit was too vague because revised plans made it effectively a new project.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice topic as listed was sufficient to inform the public that the Board would discuss Claremont’s special permit application.

allegations.summary: To the extent the complaint challenged the sufficiency of the public hearing notice, the AG declined to review it.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent the complaint alleges that a public hearing notice was insufficient or that the Board did not provide documents to the public prior to the August 10 meeting, we decline to review these allegations because, even if true, they do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: To the extent the complaint alleged the Board failed to provide documents to the public before the August 10 meeting, the AG declined to review it.
allegations.key_passage: there is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that a public body affirmatively provide copies of documents to the public before or at a meeting, or that documents be posted to a website prior to or after a meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
